ratings_why.fun: Watching the water rise across the whole Board and choosing how many seats to keep is a real draft decision every buy and sell, though early dilution and the accounting take some getting used to.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because one shared Health stat turns every buy and sell into a vote on the Level, and Under drowns weak units on both boards, your own outsiders too; no current tribe or generic auto-battler plays like that.

verdict_why: v2 closed the reading gaps (order, own Health, the Peilmeester's drowning); what is left is wording and UI, not a design fix.

points.text: The law reads well only with UI: a Board unit should show the Level as its Health and its own Health as a small 'pours X' tag, so a player knows what buying it adds.
Old Bram Stuw would read faster as 'split half your Level evenly among your surviving Board units other than this'; 'share' and 'other' can be read two ways.
The Spaarndam Pup is the best fantasy fit in the tribe but the longest text; a short face ('Damage to your Board units is shared evenly') with the Shield order in the glossary would read at a glance.
The water board's vote comes through only as seat count; one card that lets you choose to raise or lower the Level (a gavel motion) would put the procedure fantasy into play.
Damage equal to the Level kills every Under unit without a Shield, so the Peilmeester could just say they drown; the drowning would read instantly.

standouts.why: The Peilmeester of Stillwater is the seed's promise in one line: low units on both boards drown, your own outsiders too.
Levy-Master makes other tribes pay the levy, so every slot is a choice between paying water and sitting on the Board.
Aaltje Sluiswacht opening the sluice to turn water into Attack is simple to read and makes lowering the Level a vote.

weakest.why: Nest-Platform Coot is a generic token maker; its Chicks mostly dilute the Level and the floating-nest flavour does little.
Bench Coot is a plain count buff any wide tribe could print.
The Spaarndam Pup's split rules are hard to follow in a fight, even though the idea is great.

flags.note: Kobus with the Miller and Levy-Master pours about 80 a turn at Tier 5, more with goldens; linear, but the high roll to watch.
Board units tend to survive or die together, which changes hero damage; needs a playtest.
All or nothing: wipes wide boards and does nothing to a few big units.
